# Story 53 — Get support: choose a ticket or live chat

## Prerequisites

- None for this page to render. The two destinations it links to (submit-ticket form and live-chat widget) are separate stories (Story 8 in `ticket-management`, Story 14 in `live-chat`) and their routes may 404 until they land — that is expected.
- Coordinate string keys with whoever picks up Story 8 / live-chat Story 14 so the destination routes match what this page links to (`/tickets/new` and `/chat` — confirm during implementation by grepping for existing route stubs before hard-coding).

---

## Story Goal

Deliver a real customer-facing route at **`/support`** that presents two clearly-labelled options — "Start a live chat" and "Submit a ticket" — each with a one-line explanation of when to choose it, and each linking directly into the corresponding flow.

Concrete outcomes:

1. A signed-in customer visiting `/support` sees a two-card chooser with a short heading, a one-line "when to use this" description under each option, and a primary action button on each card.
2. Clicking **Start a live chat** navigates to the live-chat entry route; clicking **Submit a ticket** navigates to the submit-ticket form route. No modal, no intermediate confirmation step.
3. The customer persistent nav (rendered by `frontend/components/SiteHeader.tsx`) exposes a **"Get support"** link that lands here.
4. All copy is served through `next-intl` in both **en** and **ar** locales.
5. Page has real `<title>` / `<meta description>` (not `noindex`) via a `Metadata` export.

**Not in scope:** the submit-ticket form itself, the live-chat widget itself, agent/admin variants of this page, or any backend changes.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** No single entry point; a customer has to guess which nav link (or which page in the current draft) initiates support.
- **New behaviour:** One nav item, "Get support", lands on `/support`, which is a two-option chooser. Each card explains when to use it and goes straight into that flow when clicked.
- **Explicitly out of scope:** the submit-ticket form (Story 8), the live-chat widget (`live-chat` Story 14). This story renders the chooser page only.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Create the `/support` route

**Create file:** `frontend/app/support/page.tsx`

- Server Component. No `"use client"`.
- Read `SESSION_COOKIE`/`REFRESH_COOKIE` via `cookies()`, following `frontend/app/settings/page.tsx`'s exact pattern — not `dashboard/page.tsx` (staff-only, wrong audience) and not a `getSession()` helper (doesn't exist). On a missing access token: redirect to `/api/session/refresh?next=/support` if a refresh token exists and `_refreshed` isn't already set, else redirect to `/`. Once a valid access token is confirmed, check the role (via `peekJwtPayload` from `@/lib/jwt`, same unverified-peek-for-UI-routing use as `dashboard/page.tsx`'s `isStaff` check): if it's `agent`, `admin`, or `subadmin`, `redirect('/dashboard')` — staff aren't this page's audience.
- Load translations via `getTranslations({ namespace: 'Support' })`.
- Export `metadata: Metadata` with a real `title` and `description` sourced from the translations namespace. **Do not** set `robots: 'noindex'` — this is a signed-in-customer page, not internal admin.
- Render:
  - Page heading (`t('heading')`) and short intro paragraph (`t('intro')`).
  - Two `Card` components side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile:
    - **Live chat card:** icon + `t('liveChat.title')` + `t('liveChat.description')` + primary `Button` (as a link) labelled `t('liveChat.cta')` pointing at the live-chat route (confirm exact path during implementation; use `/chat` if no other value is discovered).
    - **Submit ticket card:** icon + `t('ticket.title')` + `t('ticket.description')` + primary `Button` (as a link) labelled `t('ticket.cta')` pointing at the submit-ticket route (use `/tickets/new` if no other value is discovered).
  - Buttons use the shadcn `<Button asChild>` + `<Link href=…>` pattern already used elsewhere in the app.

Skeleton (matches `frontend/app/settings/page.tsx`'s actual auth pattern):

```tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
import { getTranslations } from 'next-intl/server';
import { SESSION_COOKIE, REFRESH_COOKIE } from '@/lib/auth';
import { peekJwtPayload } from '@/lib/jwt';
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';

export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
  const t = await getTranslations('Support');
  return { title: t('meta.title'), description: t('meta.description') };
}

export default async function SupportPage({
  searchParams,
}: {
  searchParams: Promise<{ _refreshed?: string }>;
}) {
  const { _refreshed } = await searchParams;
  const cookieStore = await cookies();
  const accessToken = cookieStore.get(SESSION_COOKIE)?.value;
  const hasRefreshToken = Boolean(cookieStore.get(REFRESH_COOKIE)?.value);

  if (!accessToken) {
    if (hasRefreshToken && !_refreshed) redirect('/api/session/refresh?next=/support');
    redirect('/');
  }

  const { role } = peekJwtPayload(accessToken);
  const isStaff = role === 'agent' || role === 'admin' || role === 'subadmin';
  if (isStaff) redirect('/dashboard');

  const t = await getTranslations('Support');
  // …render two-card chooser…
}
```

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **No access-token cookie (routinely happens ~15min into a session, not an error)** → if a refresh-token cookie is still present, redirect to `/api/session/refresh?next=/support` for a silent refresh, guarded by the one-shot `_refreshed` search param; if that still fails, or there's no refresh token at all, redirect to `/`. Matches `frontend/app/settings/page.tsx`'s pattern exactly — do not short-circuit straight to `/login`.
- **Signed in as agent / admin / subadmin** → they are not the audience. `redirect('/dashboard')`. Enforced in the same top-of-page guard, after the access-token check succeeds.
- **Destination routes don't exist yet** (Story 8 / live-chat Story 14 not merged) → clicking a card yields Next's default 404. This is acceptable per the intake ("the links can 404 until they land"). Do **not** add a stub page for either destination.
- **RTL layout (Arabic)** → the two-card chooser must render correctly under `dir="rtl"`. Use flexbox / grid utilities that work in both directions (avoid hard-coded left/right margins in favour of `ms-*`/`me-*` or gap-based spacing).
- **Missing translation key** → `next-intl` throws in dev; adding both `en.json` and `ar.json` in the same commit prevents the "key present in en, missing in ar" runtime error.
- **Mobile viewport** → two cards must stack vertically below the `sm` (or `md`) breakpoint; the CTA buttons must remain full-width on mobile per the app's existing responsive patterns.
- **Nav duplication** → the "Get support" link must appear only in the customer nav path in `SiteHeader.tsx`, never in the staff nav array from `frontend/lib/staffNav.ts`. If both branches render the same nav, add a role guard around the new item.

## Test Plan

1. **Manual smoke — customer flow:** Sign in as a demo customer (see `backend/scripts/seed-demo-customer.ts`), verify:
   - The `SiteHeader` shows a **"Get support"** link.
   - Clicking it lands on `/support`.
   - Both cards render with correct copy; each CTA is a real `<a>` with the expected `href`.
2. **Manual smoke — locale toggle:** Toggle to Arabic via `LocaleToggleButton`, reload `/support`, verify all strings switch to Arabic and layout is RTL-correct.
3. **Manual smoke — auth guards:**
   - Log out (clears both cookies), navigate directly to `/support` → redirected to `/`.
   - Sign in as an admin (`backend/scripts/seed-admin.ts`), navigate to `/support` → redirected to `/dashboard`; the nav does **not** show "Get support".
4. **Manual smoke — metadata:** View page source on `/support`, confirm `<title>` and `<meta name="description">` reflect the translated copy and there is no `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`.
5. **Regression:** Existing routes (`/dashboard`, `/customers`, `/settings`, `/admin/users`) still render — no accidental breakage from the SiteHeader edit.

There is no existing unit-test harness for Server Component pages in `frontend/` (the test suite lives under `backend/tests/`), so this story is verified via manual smoke. If `frontend/` gains a test setup later, add a rendering test for `SupportPage` alongside the existing pattern.

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** From `frontend/`, run `npm run dev` (or `pnpm dev` — match the lockfile: `frontend/package-lock.json` implies npm). Visit `http://localhost:3000/support` while signed in as a customer.
2. **Frontend typechecks and builds:** From `frontend/`, run `npm run build`. Must complete with no TypeScript errors and no `next-intl` "missing key" warnings.
3. **Locale parity check:** Diff the top-level key sets of `frontend/messages/en.json` and `frontend/messages/ar.json` — they must be identical. Both must contain a `Support` object with the same shape.
4. **Backend builds:** From `backend/`, run `npm run build` and `npm test` to confirm no accidental impact (there should be none, but this is the project's regression floor).
5. **Regression:** Manually visit `/dashboard`, `/customers`, `/settings`, `/admin/users`, `/login` and confirm they still render as before.
